company: Gryphon Capital Income Trust (Responsible Entity: One Investment Group / OIG Holdings Pty Ltd)
title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Staff
tiers.description: OIG employees, consultants, contractors, officers and directors (including non-executive directors and External Committee Members), regardless of seniority, division or location. Subject to insider trading law (cl.4), the Embargo mechanism (cl.8.8), market manipulation (cl.10) and confidentiality (cl.11). If not also a Designated Person, may deal in Financial Products under the lighter Clause 9 regime.

tiers.name: Designated Person
tiers.description: All directors and officers of OIG Licensees and other KMP of OIG allocated to the relevant Fund; UFS KMP involved in fund administration for the Fund; all directors, officers and KMP of the Investment Manager (unless it has its own Board-acceptable trading policy); and any other person the Board designates. Subject to Clauses 5-8: Prohibited Period dealing restrictions, prior notification and clearance, an absolute margin lending ban, the short-term/speculative trading ban and short-selling ban.

tiers.name: Designated Person who is not OIG Staff
tiers.description: The subset of Designated Persons (e.g. Investment Manager directors/officers/KMP) who are not themselves OIG employees. Subject to an additional, near-total ban on dealing in financial products associated with OIG Securities (Clause 8.6), which does not apply to Designated Persons who are OIG Staff.

tiers.name: Board Members
tiers.description: Directors of an OIG Licensee that operates a Fund listed on the ASX. Must ensure ASX announcement of dealings by themselves or their Associates and inform the Director Legal, Risk & Compliance within 2 business days of the dealing.

tiers.name: Associate
tiers.description: A spouse, de facto partner, or child/step-child under 18 (Immediate Family) of a Staff Member, an SMSF for the Staff Member or Immediate Family, a private company of which either is a director, or a trust of which either is a beneficiary - being any person over whom the Staff Member has the ability to control or influence Financial Product decisions.

tiers.name: Embargoed Staff
tiers.description: Staff (including Designated Persons) nominated by the CEO to be restricted from dealing in specified Embargoed Financial Products where needed to avoid a perception of dealing with Inside Information, until that information is generally available.

definitions.hedging_definition: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: (i) has not vested; or (ii) has vested but remains subject to a holding lock

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify an extension to a closed period, or any additional period, at its discretion. Separately, the CEO may extend the policy at any time to restrict nominated Staff (Embargoed Staff, which can include Designated Persons) from dealing in specified Financial Products (Embargoed Financial Products) until Inside Information is generally available; confidentiality of this determination is not addressed.

rules.detail: Clause 5's Prohibited Period regime restricts dealing in 'OIG Securities' (Financial Products issued by an OIG Licensee and listed/quoted/traded on a Relevant Market); a derivative over those units is not itself issued by the Licensee, so it is not clearly 'OIG Securities'. The blanket ban on financial-product dealing (Clause 8.6) applies only to Designated Persons who are not OIG Staff, leaving OIG-employed Designated Persons' derivative dealing addressed only by general insider trading law.

rules.tier: Designated Person who is not OIG Staff
rules.detail: Blanket ban on dealing at any time in financial products associated with OIG Securities, expressly including derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and CFDs issued or created by third parties; only law-permitted dealing or a Clause 7 permitted dealing is excluded, and none of those exceptions covers a bank collar.
rules.evidence: deal at any time in financial products associated with OIG Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or a permitted dealing under this policy

rules.detail: Staff who are not Designated Persons may deal in Financial Products (including Securities, which by definition includes derivatives) without prior notification, approval or post-trade confirmation, provided they hold no inside information, the product is not embargoed, no conflict of interest arises and no market misconduct occurs.
rules.evidence: Staff that are not Designated Persons are permitted to deal in Financial Products (including Securities) without prior notification or approval or post-trade confirmation provided: they do not possess Inside Information

rules.tier: Designated Person who is not OIG Staff
rules.detail: Ban on transactions limiting exposure to risk on unvested remuneration; OIG states it does not remunerate Staff with OIG Securities (8.5), so this limb is most relevant to Investment Manager incentive arrangements held by non-OIG-staff Designated Persons.
rules.evidence: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: (i) has not vested

rules.tier: Designated Person who is not OIG Staff
rules.detail: Same ban extends to vested remuneration securities still subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: or (ii) has vested but remains subject to a holding lock

rules.tier: Designated Person who is not OIG Staff
rules.detail: Even once vested and unrestricted, the separate blanket ban on dealing in any financial product associated with OIG Securities continues to prohibit hedging for this tier.
rules.evidence: deal at any time in financial products associated with OIG Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or a permitted dealing under this policy

rules.detail: For an OIG-employed Designated Person, the Clause 8.6 hedging ban does not apply (it is limited to Designated Persons who are not OIG Staff), and no equity remuneration is granted by OIG (8.5), so hedging of OIG Securities by this tier is not directly addressed.

rules.tier: Designated Person who is not OIG Staff
rules.detail: Not named, but a prepaid forward or similar arrangement is a 'financial product associated with OIG Securities' and so caught by the Clause 8.6 blanket ban for this tier.
rules.evidence: Financial products include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with OIG Securities including by third parties.

rules.detail: Not named and, for OIG-employed Designated Persons, not clearly caught by the 'OIG Securities'-scoped Prohibited Period regime (see derivatives topic).
Applies to all Designated Persons regardless of OIG-employment status, and extends to Financial Products associated with the Fund or OIG Securities.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short-selling or speculative trading of OIG Securities or in Financial Products associated with the relevant Fund or OIG Securities.

rules.detail: The short-selling ban (8.4) is expressed only for Designated Persons.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.

rules.tier: Designated Person who is not OIG Staff
rules.detail: Contracts for difference are expressly named as a Financial Product caught by the Clause 8.6 blanket ban for this tier.
rules.evidence: Financial products include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with OIG Securities including by third parties.

rules.detail: CFDs fall within 'Financial Products'; Staff who are not Designated Persons may deal in them under the Clause 9 conditions.
rules.evidence: Staff that are not Designated Persons are permitted to deal in Financial Products (including Securities) without prior notification or approval or post-trade confirmation

rules.detail: Absolute ban, applying to all Designated Persons regardless of OIG-employment status, with no clearance route; grounded in the risk that margin loan terms could force a sale during a Prohibited Period or while holding inside information.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to OIG Securities.

rules.detail: The margin lending ban does not extend to other funding arrangements where OIG Securities are included as security; a Designated Person should (but is not required to) consult Director Legal, Risk & Compliance if uncertain about the classification of an arrangement.
rules.evidence: The restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where OIG Securities may be included as security. Designated Persons should consult Director Legal, Risk & Compliance if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: Only 'margin lending arrangements' are banned outright; a non-margin secured financing arrangement using OIG Securities as security is expressly carved out and permitted, subject to the general insider trading and Prohibited Period rules applying to any resulting sale of the underlying units.
rules.evidence: The restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where OIG Securities may be included as security.

rules.detail: Twelve-month minimum holding period for OIG Securities and for Financial Products associated with the Fund or OIG Securities, i.e. longer than the 6-month period used in many other ASX policies and extending to derivative-type instruments.
rules.evidence: OIG encourages Designated Persons to be long term investors in Funds and to hold OIG Securities for 12 months or more and Designated Persons must avoid short term (less than 12 months) trading in OIG Securities or in Financial Products associated with the relevant Fund or OIG Securities.

clearance.approver: Notification Officer (Director Legal, Risk & Compliance; or CEO/Chairman of the Compliance Committee if the Director Legal, Risk & Compliance is the one dealing)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 3 business days from when the dealing occurred
clearance.evidence: If the proposed dealing by the Designated Person would be in a Prohibited Period, before dealing in the Securities, the Designated Person must receive a written clearance ... A clearance expires five business days from its date, unless the Clearance Notice specifies a different expiry date.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as practicable and within 2 business days of the dealing
clearance.evidence: Directors must as soon as practicable, and within 2 business days of the dealing, inform the Director Legal Risk & Compliance providing sufficient detail of the dealing to allow the required announcement be made to the ASX.

short_term.evidence: OIG encourages Designated Persons to be long term investors in Funds and to hold OIG Securities for 12 months or more and Designated Persons must avoid short term (less than 12 months) trading in OIG Securities or in Financial Products associated with the relevant Fund or OIG Securities.

exemption_authority: The Notification Officer determines whether Exceptional Circumstances exist (hardship, court order, or other circumstances as the CEO or Compliance Committee Chairman decides), permitting dealing at any time without notification, approval or clearance, subject always to insider trading law; the Notification Officer is directed to 'exercise their discretion with caution' if in doubt.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin loan ban does not extend to other secured financing
bespoke_clauses.clause: The restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where OIG Securities may be included as security. Designated Persons should consult Director Legal, Risk & Compliance if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on the collared shares, if not structured as a classic margin loan, falls outside the absolute margin-lending ban and is not otherwise expressly regulated - the only step suggested is an optional consultation with Compliance on classification.

bespoke_clauses.topic: blanket derivatives ban for non-OIG-staff Designated Persons
bespoke_clauses.clause: Subject to the law, Designated Persons who are not OIG Staff must not ... deal at any time in financial products associated with OIG Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or a permitted dealing under this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar counterparty is a Designated Person who is not an OIG employee (e.g. an external Investment Manager director), the put/call legs are prohibited outright with no clearance route available.

bespoke_clauses.topic: possible gap for OIG-employed Designated Persons
bespoke_clauses.clause: OIG Securities: Financial Products issued by an OIG Licensee and listed, quoted or traded on a Relevant Market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because a bespoke OTC derivative is not itself 'issued by' the OIG Licensee, an OIG-employed Designated Person's collar may not be clearly caught by either the Prohibited Period regime or the Clause 8.6 ban (limited to non-OIG-staff); this should be confirmed with Compliance rather than assumed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender (or financier) exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement where such agreements are prohibited by this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Provided the bank's facility is not a 'margin lending agreement', its enforcement sale of the collared units is expressly excluded from the Prohibited Period ban and needs no prior notification or clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: OIG does not remunerate its Staff with OIG Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no unvested or holding-locked incentive stock issued by OIG itself; any OIG-employed collar candidate would be dealing in already-vested, open-market-acquired units.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must avoid short term (less than 12 months) trading in OIG Securities or in Financial Products associated with the relevant Fund or OIG Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entering or unwinding a collar within 12 months of acquiring the underlying units could itself be characterised as prohibited short-term trading, independent of the derivative-specific analysis above.

summary: Whether a funded collar is possible turns on the counterparty's employment status and how the loan is structured. If the director/executive is a Designated Person who is not an OIG employee (e.g. an external Investment Manager director), the put/call legs are banned outright by the Clause 8.6 blanket prohibition on dealing in any financial product associated with OIG Securities, including third-party derivatives, with no available clearance. If they are an OIG-employed Designated Person, the derivative legs fall into a structural gap, since the Prohibited Period/clearance regime is keyed to 'OIG Securities' (units issued by the Licensee and market-traded), which a bespoke OTC derivative is not - this should be confirmed with Compliance rather than relied upon. The loan leg is more favourable in either case: the margin lending ban is expressly limited to 'margin lending arrangements', and the policy confirms this 'does not extend to other funding arrangements where OIG Securities may be included as security', so a bespoke secured loan is permitted (with only an optional advisory consultation), and a lender's enforcement sale is an express, clearance-free exception to the Prohibited Period rules provided the facility is not itself a margin loan. Short selling and margin lending are absolutely banned for all Designated Persons regardless of employment status, and a 12-month minimum holding period applies to both the underlying units and related financial products.
